title: Global Investment Committee 2020 Outlook | Morgan Stanley
description: 2020 could prove to be a decent year for investors, but it may include some bumps along the way. Here's some important advice for navigating this year's markets. https://mgstn.ly/2G5RQkZ

asr.full_text: Coming off of a remarkable year for stocks in 2019, what's in store for investors in 2020? We don't expect another banner year in the US, but globally growth should rebound. And that should create investment opportunities in non-US securities. Why the lukewarm outlook for the US? While monetary policy is currently accommodative, we see the rebound in growth is moderate, as the U.S. consumer is already spending near peak rates and corporations are facing headwinds to profits. The Federal Reserve wants a certain level of inflation. That means a weaker U.S. dollar, which is good for exporters, but contributes to inflation and would offset any benefit to consumers if there were a de-escalation of trade tensions. Be selective in 2020. With the U.S. economy expected to slow while the rest of the world recovers at a faster pace, we think investors should look to active management, emphasizing non-U.S. markets, defensive sectors, and high-quality, reasonably priced companies. As 2019 showed, a year can make a significant difference in returns. Position your portfolio for 2020.
